pcp-expository-colour-polynomials|PCP.Al.annotation: The existence claim adds a degree ceiling to the fixed-polynomial argument. Starting from a colouring, interpolation (Section 3) bounds the degree in each coordinate by $|H|-1$. Starting from a witness polynomial, restriction to the grid gives the colouring.

pcp-expository-hadamard|PCP.Algebraic.BL.annotation: BLR estimates distance to a linear map on the label space. A linear map can still send the constant label to the wrong bit or fail to respect label products, which is why the Hadamard test of Theorem 7.2 adds checks for those properties.

pcp-expository-binary-tests|PCP.Algebrai.annotation: With $J\kappa$ below the point-versus-line threshold (Theorem 6.1), a single decoded polynomial gives both conclusions. Full-label distance controls masked reads of composed labels, and distance on homogeneous linear labels controls the linear comparisons.

pcp-expository-soundness|PCP.Algebraic.T.annotation: If rejection is below the gap, the low-degree branches first give four nearby polynomials (Theorem 8.1). The remaining checks force the two vanishing identities and the consistency of the difference polynomial, so those polynomials yield a colouring. The field and degree comparisons in the statement are needed to make the error bounds smaller than the ideal rejection bounds.

linked-source-19|PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColo.annotation: The formal clause gives the query and seed budgets in terms of $R$, with soundness $1/2$ after repetition. The numerical single-run gap is established in the fair-bit sampling analysis in Section 10.

pcp-long-intro-theorem|PCP.np_subset_pcp.annotation: Lean fixes an exact logarithmic seed budget and a polynomial bound on the reachable addresses in addition to a constant query bound. The address bound supplies the finite prefix used by the converse (Theorem 1.2), even when the proof oracle is presented as a function on all natural numbers.

pcp-long-grid-constraints|PCP.Algebraic..annotation: `colorable_iff_exists_constraints` turns the fixed-polynomial argument into an existence theorem with the additional degree cap. Interpolation (Lemma 2.2) gives that cap for the extension of a colouring, and restricting any polynomial satisfying both identities gives the reverse implication.

pcp-long-intro-roadmap|PCP.Algebraic.Gri.annotation: The degree ceiling on the certificate is needed to encode its honest line restrictions below the digit cutoff (Lemma 3.3). On the grid the two identities alone force $A(X)=M(X,0)=0$. The nonempty-grid premise lets the forward construction retain the degree ceiling.

pcp-long-binary-test-statement|PCP.Algeb.annotation: The small-error condition is on $J_c\kappa$ because the binary test must first be compared with the field-valued point-versus-line test (Theorem 4.8). Both conclusion clauses use the same polynomial, with homogeneous error needed separately for later linear tests.

pcp-long-zero-on-grid-statement|PCP.Alge.annotation: The derived constraint is required to be represented by a polynomial of degree at most $D_1$. The label-degree premise permits a composed query, and the two queries of a masked read contribute $2\varepsilon$ (Equation (B24)) before the certificate-correction factor is applied.

pcp-long-soundness-statement|PCP.Algebra.annotation: The lower bound applies to every received eight-table proof. The field-size comparison is used to decode the point-versus-line data, and the separate comparison involving $|H|$ limits the Schwartz–Zippel (Lemma 2.1) loss after substitution of the grid vanishing polynomials.

pcp-long-proof-map-correction|PCP.Algebr.annotation: The correction estimate of Proposition 5.6 is for one prescribed target. It counts rejection and a wrong returned bit together and charges the corrector’s rejection rate at that target. The two calls in the grid test are handled by averaging this estimate at their respective targets.

pcp-long-reference-np|PCP.ReferenceNP.in.annotation: `inNP_iff_mem` applies in both directions for every language. It lets a reference NP membership hypothesis enter the verifier construction and identifies the concrete witness class produced by the converse (Theorem 1.2) with the same reference class.

pcp-long-algebra-agreement-boost|PCP.Alg.annotation: The coarse closeness bound (Equation (A19)) is used to show that disagreeing degree-$d$ slices cannot occur too often. The threshold involving $2d/q$ accounts for the possible roots of a difference on a row and a column. Adding the original table-to-row error yields $4\varepsilon$.

pcp-long-algebra-point-line-constants|PC.annotation: The single premise $q\ge10^6d^3$ supplies the bivariate field bound (Theorem 4.7), the conditions for reparametrization and line characterization, and the numerical crossing inequality (Equation (A26)). Positive $d$ is what yields the absolute floor of $10^6$.

pcp-long-blr-proof|PCP.Algebraic.BLR.exi.annotation: The conclusion gives a linear functional on the space of labels, with no small-error threshold. A linear functional on labels need not be evaluation at a binary message. The unit and product tests in Theorem 5.2 are what later enforce that extra property.

pcp-long-binary-weighted-test|PCP.Algebr.annotation: The result upgrades rowwise field decoding to one polynomial using the weighted low-degree test. Both distances use the same polynomial, and the constant is large enough to cover rejection above the range of the small-error theorem (Theorem 4.4) by the trivial bound on distance.

pcp-long-encoded-line-soundness|PCP.Alge.annotation: The small-error premise is on the comparison between the decoded lines and the decoded point function. The resulting point polynomial is used for both distance bounds. The $28$ term in $S_c$ comes from decoding the original point rows (Corollary 5.3).

pcp-long-zero-on-grid-soundness|PCP.Alge.annotation: Lean divides the grid inequality by $1+2C_c>0$ to bound the rejection rate itself. The two correction calls (each controlled by Equation (B16)) give the factor two on certificate-table distance. Substituting the grid vanishing polynomials can increase degree by a factor of $|H|$, which explains the field-size term.

pcp-short-abstract|PCP.np_subset_pcp|1.annotation: The verifier, machine implementation and constants are chosen once for the language. The polynomial in `ReadsBelow` bounds the largest possible proof address even when later queries depend on earlier answers, which lets the converse in Section 7 use a finite witness.

pcp-short-proof-table-type|PCP.Algebraic.annotation: The `Proof` fields are functions returning bits at typed addresses. There is no consistency premise between a points table and its lines table, so the soundness theorem (Theorem 6.1) can start with arbitrary received answers.

pcp-short-outer-decoding|PCP.Algebraic.E.annotation: The bound on $J\kappa$ puts the decoded point-versus-line data in the small-error range (Theorem 4.5). The conclusion estimates two distances to the same polynomial of degree at most $cb^c$, giving both the full-label control used in composed reads and the homogeneous control used in linear checks.

pcp-short-zero|PCP.Algebraic.BinaryZeroO.annotation: If $A$ is nonzero somewhere on the grid, the two certificate identities cannot both be polynomial identities. The Schwartz–Zippel bound in Section 2 and a random homogeneous label give the left-hand bound. The two certificate reads (each controlled by Equation (14)) account for the factor two on $\delta_M$ and the two contributions to the correction cost.

pcp-short-derived-zero|PCP.Algebraic.Der.annotation: The composed label need not be uniform, so the verifier reads at a uniform mask and at its translate by the composed label (Lemma 3.4). Each read contributes at most $\epsilon$ of full-label error. The degree bound $r$ ensures that the composed label is in the table.

linked-source-12|PCP.Algebraic.ThreeColo.annotation: With the certificate identities supplied directly, every honest read satisfies the check it enters. The strict degree premises allow exact recovery of each honest line restriction under the encoding substitution (Equation (4)). The theorem takes a seed as an arbitrary argument, so the same proof works for all seeds.

pcp-short-reference-np|PCP.ReferenceNP.i.annotation: The equivalence transports the two PCP implications to the reference definition of NP. The machine-to-checker direction supplies the hypothesis of Theorem 1.1, and the checker-to-machine direction converts the output of the converse in Section 7 to reference NP membership.
